flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk in Chromium at 1440x900 and 390x844. The most prominent action in the first screen at both widths is the dark submit button 'Get alerts for my neighbourhood' in the hero form #signup (1440: y=690, 306x57; 390: y=628, full width); its repeat is #signup-2. I confirmed the flag's premise that nothing before the click says sign-up is not connected: the note under each button reads 'Always free. One email per meeting, only when something matches. Unsubscribe in one click...', and no visible page text mentions 'not connected' or a missing list. Operating both forms at both widths: an empty submit shows 'Choose a neighbourhood first.'; choosing Eastside and entering resident@example.com shows a status box right under the button (at 1440 it starts at y=869, inside the viewport): 'Not sent yet. Sign-up is not connected to a mailing list, so nothing left this page and your address was not stored. When the pilot list is live, this button will subscribe resident@example.com to Eastside alerts.' There were no network requests, no navigation, no mailto/URL/phone and no console or page errors. Against the table: the button responds visibly, so it does not 'do nothing'. It throws no error and points to no missing file or anchor. It does not go to a contact or URL the brief did not supply. It reports the opposite of success ('Not sent yet... was not stored'), so the false-success clause does not apply. 'Get alerts for my neighbourhood' names an action, not a destination, so the 'Read the docs that scrolls the page' clause does not apply, and the brief itself says sign-up has no backend yet. The pre-commit exemption would only matter if a Counts clause were met, and none is. The missing up-front notice is an honesty and interaction issue to score, not HF1.
